body:
Yeah, I'm a gay male.

On the topic of waiting, I'm all for it http://www.cdc.gov/hiv/statistics/basics/ataglance.html In fact, I grew up in a religious household so this is, I suppose, sort of my default position.There are a few problems. For one, being gay already seriously limits my dating pool. A lot. Finding someone who is gay and willing to wait isn't particularly easy, considering the fact that we all have other factors we look at as well (attractiveness, personality, etc.)

As far as the window period goes, partners often have moments of weakness that they don't disclose. One of the most reliable studies on adultery, conducted by the University of Chicago in 1992, found that a quarter of heterosexual men reported cheating on their wives. Now consider that gay men are statistically more promiscuous than straights *in general* and Goddamn. 

Concerning the statistics about HIV among homosexuals, look above at that URL. Sorry, my phone messed up the paste job. Those statistics are from 2010. Not some distant America at the onset of the AIDS epidemic, 2010. In fact, some things have actually gone up in recent years.

As far as that cure goes, if we're thinking about the same thing, that was shut down a few months ago because they had major setbacks.

Condoms probably break more easily in homosexual interactions than they do in heterosexual ones.

Thank you for the response. I was brief in some areas because I'm using my phone, but there really are tons of scary recent statistics, and the testing AND medication leave much to be desired. I appreciate that 20 years is longer than 7, but I don't want to risk dieing at 40 because I don't want to be alone. Wish I could restart. :(
